physical_harm: Victim died; PW-1 suffered injuries during intervention
number_of_offences: Charged under Sections 148, 302, 324 read with Sec.149; only appellant was upheld
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the evidence of PW-1, medical evidence, and the test identification parade, and held that the incident was the outcome of a sudden quarrel, falling within Exception 4 to Section 300 of the IPC.
witness_credibility: The court assessed PW-1 as a credible witness, noting that his presence at the incident was fortified by the injuries found on his person, and that there was no evidence to suggest he was completely inebriated.
trial_duration: Offence: 4th November 1991; Trial judgment: 2.2.2005; High Court decision: 769 of 1996; Supreme Court decision: March 30, 2011
legal_representation: Raju Ragupathi, C. Paramasivam, P. Ramesh, M.P. Parthiban, Rakesh K. Sharma for the Appellant; D V. Kanagraj, V.G. Pragasam, S.J. Aristotle, S. Prabu Ramasubramanian, Vipin Jai for the Respondent
investigation_status: FIR registered on 5th November 1991; charge sheet filed; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Acquittal; High Court: Reversed acquittal of appellant; Supreme Court: Dismissed appeal
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the High Court's reversal of the Trial Court's acquittal of the appellant was justified, as the evidence of PW-1, medical evidence, and test identification parade supported the conviction. They also emphasized that the incident was a sudden quarrel, falling under Exception 4 to Section 300 of the IPC, and that the sentence of three years R.I. was appropriate given the circumstances.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the High Court's reliance on PW-1's testimony was not acceptable, especially since PW-2 and PW-4 were hostile witnesses. They also doubted the reliability of the test identification parade, suggesting that the dim lighting and the inebriated state of PW-1 made identification impossible. They further claimed that the sentence should be reduced as the incident occurred many years ago.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the High Court's reversal of the Trial Court's acquittal was justified if the Trial Court's judgment was perverse and contrary to the evidence on record. It also considered the legal principle of Exception 4 to Section 300 of the IPC for sudden quarrels.
sentencing_rationale: The High Court imposed a sentence of three years R.I. considering that the incident occurred 15 years earlier and the appellant had a mentally challenged brother to look after, which was deemed to serve the ends of justice.
judicial_mitigating_factors: The appellant had a mentally challenged brother to look after, which was considered a mitigating factor in determining the sentence.
